rule: Four separated, single-colour, 8-connected pieces on black are rotated (never mirrored) parts of an NxN square, where N*N is the number of coloured cells. The 7 piece also holds the single 5. The output is the unique reassembly with the 5 at the top-left cell and each piece covering exactly one of the four corners.
scope: Partition a square into four connected corner-owning pieces with interlocking tabs; rotate and scatter them without touching; enforce one valid assembly with marker5 at top-left of the7 piece.

authored_scope: Sampled answers are N in 4..14 (explicit size 4..16; an explicit square may have N up to 21, limited by area). Each answer is built from a quadrant cut with at least one interlocking tab, and the pieces are randomly rotated and scattered without touching on a black input. The input is 20x20 often, as in all fixtures, and other sizes up to 30x30 are synthetic extensions with input area > 2*N*N. Not supported: piece counts other than four, mirrored pieces, non-black backgrounds, a marker other than 5 or a marker piece colour other than 7, and non-quadrant topologies (for example, a piece that touches no split line).
authored_constraints: Exactly four pieces; each piece is 8-connected, single-coloured (the 7 piece also includes the 5 cell), has at least 3 cells and owns exactly one corner of the square.
The 5 appears exactly once, at output[0][0].
The pieces admit exactly one assembly with the 5 at the top-left and four distinct corner owners. This is checked by bounded enumeration on both the random and the explicit-square paths.
In the input, no two pieces overlap or touch, even diagonally, so diagonal component extraction recovers exactly the four pieces. This holds for random and explicit placements.
Input area is strictly greater than 2*N*N, so black is the strict majority colour.
The three non-7 colours are distinct values from {1,2,3,4,6,8,9}; bools are rejected as ints.
Random partitions contain at least one interlocking tab.
